label: rr-diagonalisation
tail:
- [The annihilator theorem](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-minimal-polynomial-is-well-defined-and-controls-annihilators.md:26) begins “For every endomorphism … of a finite-dimensional \(F\)-vector space.”
   - [The minimal-polynomial criterion](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-diagonalisable-iff-minimal-polynomial-splits-with-distinct-roots.md:26) has the same finite-dimensional domain.
   - The library’s [definition of diagonalisable](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-diagonalisable-endomorphism.md:25) is itself stated only for finite-dimensional spaces.

   Thus `[L1]` and `[L2]` enlarge their cited domains, and step 1.1 applies them without their load-bearing hypothesis. The direct-sum/projection portion of the proof works in arbitrary dimension, but the diagonalisability conclusion then requires bases for the two summands—a choice issue not addressed by the item.

   The cited Conrad treatment also sets finite-dimensionality as an ambient hypothesis before its idempotent corollary. [Keith Conrad, *The Minimal Polynomial and Some Applications*](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/minpolyandappns.pdf)

   **Severity: fatal.** The title and Statement assert more than the supplied proof and cited results establish.

## Nonfatal findings

2. **`thm-diagonalisable-iff-characteristic-polynomial-splits-and-multiplicities-agree`, `[L6]`**

   `[L6]` states a result about the characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism, but its cited [lemma](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-characteristic-polynomial-is-monic-and-has-extreme-coefficients.md:30) states the result only for matrices. The transport is licensed immediately by `[L5]`, the [operator definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-characteristic-polynomial-of-an-operator.md:31), but `[L6]` does not cite that bridge.

   **Severity: nonfatal.** Immediate definition-unfolding.

3. **Same item, proof step 2.1**

   The step says that concatenating bases of the eigenspaces is independent “by `[L3]`.” The cited [theorem](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-eigenvectors-for-distinct-eigenvalues-are-linearly-independent.md:29) covers one eigenvector for each pairwise distinct eigenvalue, whereas the concatenation can contain several vectors with the same eigenvalue. One must first group a putative relation into vectors \(w_\lambda\in E_\lambda(T)\), apply `[L3]` to the nonzero \(w_\lambda\), and then use independence within each eigenspace basis.

   **Severity: nonfatal.** This is a sub-30-second bridge.

4. **`thm-diagonalisable-iff-minimal-polynomial-splits-with-distinct-roots`, proof step 2.1**

   From `[L3]`, the step obtains \(x-\lambda_i\mid\mu_T\) separately for every \(i\), then immediately concludes that their product divides \(\mu_T\). That requires the omitted observation that the distinct linear factors are pairwise coprime, followed by Euclid’s lemma or unique factorisation. Neither appears among the step’s declared inputs.

   **Severity: nonfatal.** The missing coprimeness argument is routine and comfortably within the 30-second threshold.

5. **`thm-simultaneous-diagonalisation-of-commuting-diagonalisable-endomorphisms`, proof step 1.2**

   The step says `[L3]` makes \(U=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal T)\) finite-dimensional. `[L3]` only states that the ambient space \(\mathcal L(V,V)\) is finite-dimensional; the required bridge is that a subspace of a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional, supplied by [this theorem](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace.md:37), which is not cited by the item.

   **Severity: nonfatal.** Standard one-line subspace reasoning.

No other fatal defect was found.
